plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, fragrant clusters of tiny star-shaped flowers weigh down the branches and perfume the air of spring gardens, parks and old farmyards. Bees and butterflies crowd the blooms on warm afternoons.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring, typically May in cool temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across the northeastern United States, southern Canada and northern and central Europe
plants.funFact: Lilac is a member of the olive family. Each tiny flower has four petals, and finding a five-petaled one is traditionally considered good luck.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Lush, ruffled blooms as big as saucers open above glossy, deeply cut leaves. They release a sweet, rose-like scent and are among the most loved cut flowers of late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer, with peak bloom from May to June in temperate climates
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia and Siberia, and widely grown in gardens across temperate North America, Europe and East Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live for more than 50 years in the same spot, and ants are often seen on the buds. They sip the sweet nectar and do not harm the flower.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This is a winter-blooming shrub that fills Southern Hemisphere gardens with delicate, silky flowers. Its blooms often appear against dark, glossy evergreen foliage as the air turns cooler.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, roughly April to July in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens in Australia and New Zealand, originally from Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to make a cooking and lamp oil in Japan.
